family.description: This repeat has no known function. It is about 35 amino acids long and found in up to 18 copies in some proteins. This family appears to be greatly expanded in plants. This repeat occurs in PET309 [swissprot:P32522] that may be involved in RNA stabilisation [[cite:PUB00001271]]. This domain occurs in crp1 that is involved in RNA processing [[cite:PUB00001258]]. This repeat is associated with a predicted plant protein [swissprot:O49549] that has a domain organisation similar to the human BRCA1 protein. The repeat has been called PPR [[cite:PUB00017589]].
family.name: PPR repeat

causal_graphs.context: Purified N-terminal thioredoxin and C-terminal six-His fusions are titrated against 250 pM radiolabeled Dd120 RNA, a 120-nt psbH-region probe. Reactions use 20 ul, 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 40 mM KCl, 6 mM MgCl2, 0.05 mM EDTA, 2 mM DTT and 8% w/v glycerol at 25 C for 15 min, followed by 10% native PAGE. Apparent K_D is the protein concentration at 50% total RNA binding; the competitive-assay extra salt/heparin is not part of this condition.

evidence.explanation: Figure 3B's WT and 5-K12N values, the mutation Results and gel-shift Methods establish the loss-of-binding comparison. The retained direction follows the figure and operational definition, not the text's reversed K_D wording.
Current sequence matching places locally mapped K426 inside PF01535 while preserving the different old motif convention and unresolved complete assay constructs.
evidence.snippet: Q9SF38 Pfam:PF01535; repeat intervals: 416-442 and 559-585, inclusive.

edges.mechanism: The 5-K12N fusion requires more than 2500 nM protein to reach the operational half-binding threshold, compared with 9.7 nM for WT. This supports reduced binding in the tested assay, not complete absence of every RNA interaction.
edges.subject: motif5-k12n-versus-wt

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure 3B and its Results explicitly compare the 5-K12N single mutant with the 5-K12N/6-N12K double mutant. N464 lies outside the current PF01535 hit, so this is a fusion-context rescue rather than an isolated-domain claim.

edges.mechanism: On the 5-K12N background, adding 6-N12K lowers the operational half-binding concentration from above 2500 nM to 384.6 nM. The comparison is to the single mutant, not WT; this is partial recovery and does not prove a particular inter-residue contact.
edges.subject: motif6-n12k-on-k12n

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Q9SF38 / HCF152 / At3g09650 is the 778-aa Arabidopsis reference, sequence version 1, identical between UniProt and InterPro. Current PF01535 hits are 416-442 and 559-585. Local Figure 2C motif residues identify 5-K12 as reference K426 inside the first hit and 6-N12 as N464 outside both current hits. Historical motif numbering is not the same as current Pfam boundaries. Complete mini-protein endpoints and linkers remain unverified because supplementary primers were inaccessible.
causal_graphs.limitations: Directness concerns the purified fusion's net binding response, not a proven atomic RNA contact or isolated PF01535 sufficiency. Multiple shifted species limit equilibrium interpretation. Figures 2/3 were visually inspected; supplemental gels, purity and primers were not. Independent purification batches and mutant-folding equivalence remain unestablished. The double mutant remains much weaker than WT; no cellular processing or editing chain is inferred.

causal_graphs.scope: Arabidopsis HCF152-derived HCF/5&6 mini-protein fusions in Kobayashi 2012 Figure 3B; not full-length chloroplast protein or all PPR proteins.
causal_graphs.title: Motif-5 K12N reduces RNA binding and motif-6 N12K partly restores it

causal_graphs.context: Dd120 RNA at 250 pM is incubated with serial protein concentrations in 20 ul containing 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 40 mM KCl, 6 mM MgCl2, 0.05 mM EDTA, 2 mM DTT and 8% w/v glycerol, for 15 min at 25 C. Native 10% PAGE supplies the operational 50%-binding concentration; no extra competitive-assay salt or heparin is assumed.

evidence.explanation: Figure 3B's 6-N12R and WT rows were visually checked against the Results and assay definition; an unquantified ND value is not treated as zero binding.

edges.mechanism: The 6-N12R fusion has an apparent half-binding concentration above 2500 nM versus 9.7 nM for WT. This supports reduced assay binding despite introducing an additional basic residue; no specific physical explanation is uniquely established.
edges.subject: motif6-n12r-versus-wt

evidence.explanation: Visually inspected Figure 3B and mutation Results support partial recovery on the N12R background. This does not establish that a universal paired-residue code or K12M alone causes the same result.

edges.mechanism: Adding 5-K12M to 6-N12R lowers the operational half-binding concentration from above 2500 nM to 454.5 nM. The observed improvement remains far from WT and is limited to this double-versus-single-mutant comparison.
edges.subject: motif5-k12m-on-n12r

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Local motif sequence mapping to Q9SF38 places 6-N12 at N464 outside current PF01535 and 5-K12 at K426 within 416-442. Q9SF38 also has a separate 559-585 PF01535 hit, not this motif-5/6 pair. These are perturbations of the same mapped-protein-derived fusion, not proof that each perturbed residue belongs to the current Pfam hit. Historical full clone boundaries remain unresolved.
causal_graphs.limitations: The N12R effect is outside the current Pfam interval and may involve the broader fusion context. The matched double-mutant comparison does not independently establish an isolated K12M effect. No direct RNA-contact geometry, universal basic/neutral residue rule, native chloroplast effect or folding equivalence is established. Supplemental gels and primer table remain inaccessible.

This repeat occurs in PET309 [swissprot:P32522] that may be involved in RNA stabilisation [[cite:PUB00001271]]. This domain occurs in crp1 that is involved in RNA processing [[cite:PUB00001258]]. evidence.explanation: Main Methods, relevant Results/Discussion and Figures 2/3 support four scoped mutation comparisons. Supplement Table S1 and Figures S1/S3/S4 were inaccessible; purity, complete constructs, underlying gels and a definitive residue-contact interpretation remain open. Figure 3B puts K12H at 27 nM versus WT 9.7 nM; it is not literally unchanged.

Pet309 deletion/translation work is a separate lead. The tested D273-10B derivatives differ from the S288c reference context, and the inspected current P32522 Pfam assignments contain PF23276 rather than PF01535. Its PPR annotation is not sufficient to transfer those deletion phenotypes into this family graph.

discussions.notes: Assess other PPR members and full-length HCF152 perturbations from their own primary evidence. Do not repair the source's reversed K_D wording silently or treat an inaccessible supplement as negative evidence. Partial scientific self-review; IN_PROGRESS.

discussions.rationale: Local K426 mapping is supported, but old repeat definitions, present Pfam hits and full fusion boundaries are different claims. Binding changes do not automatically establish native RNA processing, translation or editing mechanisms.
